_about: SRC-9 registry of connector gate coverage. One entry per connector type that connector_type lists as supported after all migrations (0035, 0043, 0062, 0066, 0096). 'gate' names the ops/ gate that covers the type today, or null. Each step (connect, discover, load, reload) is 'real' (the product does it and the gate must see it work), 'refused' (the product answers an honest not_supported failure today and the gate must see exactly that; the reason is the backlog item that will change it) or 'missing' (no gate asserts it yet). Read by the gates through ops/gates/gate_summary.py, which turns it and the results into the table in the CI job summary, and by the coverage check of SRC-9 task 8. Change it in the same commit as the gate or the product behaviour it describes. For change-capture types load is the first copy and reload is a later insert, update and delete arriving. A type that is supported but not fully covered may carry an explicit 'waiver' {until: backlog id, reason}; the coverage check lists it as waived and fails on a waiver that waives nothing. The g6 gate is one script run by two CI jobs, g6-ingest (G6_GROUP=sql) and g6-ingest-other (G6_GROUP=other); this registry names gates, not jobs, so every type the script loads keeps 'g6' and each job's table shows the other job's types as skipped, 'covered by job <name>'. The g6-saas gate is likewise one script run by two CI jobs (g6-saas-a: HubSpot, Zendesk, Salesforce, Google Analytics 4, ServiceNow; g6-saas-b: Confluence, SharePoint, Dynamics 365, and the unsupported Workday Reports and NetSuite, which have no entry here until a real-account test); each entry's note names its job.

notes.all: SRC-9 plan task 3: mariadb:11.4 in the g6 override. MariaDB uses the MySQL driver (wire driver 'mysql'), so connect and discover go through the same code paths as MySQL.

notes.discover: SRC-13 D12: the schemas hold dbo; the preview of dbo.orders shows id and amount with declared types.
SRC-13 D12: the list under the glob landing/*.csv holds landing/orders.csv with its size, and its preview shows id, customer and amount, types inferred from the first rows.
SRC-13 D12: the list is the dial's endpoints and holds /items; the orchestrator's preview of the first page shows id and name, types inferred. The load names the endpoint (D3).

notes.all: SRC-9 plan task 5, SRC-4 T1.2 to T1.5: ops/g6/g6_oracle_test.py in its own job (g6-oracle), against Oracle Database Free (gvenzl/oracle-free, slim-faststart) in ops/g6/docker-compose.g6-oracle.override.yml. The connector dials over TLS (tcps, sslServerCertDn, a CA the gate generates) to a TLS front of the listener (nginx stream), so Oracle's own TCPS endpoint and wallet are not exercised.
notes.connect: SRC-4 T1.1: the API has no Oracle client, so POST .../test launches the test in the orchestrator (discover_job, kind test) and answers pending; the gate reads the result from GET .../discovery/test and the probe history: a pass with the orchestrator's latency, a wrong password (sign_in_refused) and a closed port (unreachable) with their fixed sentences and an unhealthy connector.
notes.discover: SRC-13 D12: the orchestrator lists the schemas the login can read (G6_INGEST among them) and that schema's tables (G6_INGEST.ORDERS); the preview shows the declared columns ID, AMOUNT and NOTE. The load's source object is the listed name.
notes.load: SRC-4 T1.2, T1.3: the source object is saved with column choice (NOTE left out, spelled as the preview spells it) and the incremental load mode with the cursor ID; Bronze has id and amount and no note.
notes.reload: SRC-4 T1.3: two rows inserted at the source, a second run reads exactly those two (the run record says so) and Bronze holds all five.

notes.connect: SRC-5: a MongoDB connector cannot be tested from the console.
notes.discover: SRC-13 D12: the orchestrator lists the collections of g6_ingest, which hold orders; its preview of up to 100 documents shows id and amount, types inferred.

notes.connect: SRC-5: a Kafka connector cannot be tested from the console.
notes.discover: SRC-13 D12: the orchestrator lists the broker's topics, which hold the one the run reads; its preview of the last messages shows id and amount, types inferred. Asked after the run, so the topic exists and holds messages.
notes.reload: A micro-batch: the gate produces a known number of new messages before the second run and expects the table to grow by exactly the messages the consumer group had not yet committed.

notes.all: SRC-9 plan task 4: atmoz/sftp in the g6 override, with a host key minted by the fixture so the pinned fingerprint is its own.
notes.connect: SRC-5: an SFTP connector cannot be tested from the console.
